result.summary: This PR hardens the wallet migration-to-sqlite path so that failures during migration are caught and reported gracefully instead of crashing or leaving the wallet in a state that needs manual restoration. It unifies watchonly/solvables wallet creation, catches exceptions from wallet creation and descriptor addition, avoids aborting on non-writable directories, and defers deleting the original BDB database until the new sqlite database is fully built. It follows up on two previously merged robustness fixes (#34156, #34176) after the author found more edge cases.
result.problem: Users migrating a legacy wallet to sqlite can hit exceptions or filesystem errors mid-migration that crash the process or leave the wallet database in a state requiring manual backup restoration, which is confusing and risky for average users.

open_concerns: ryanofsky noted the last commit ('make sqlite creation robust') is a mixed bag: it delays deletion of the original wallet (good) but adds complexity and leaves two copies of the database temporarily; he suggested a simpler long-term redesign (rename-based) but did not block on it
Several detailed inline suggestions from ryanofsky about exception safety of filesystem calls, symlink handling, and cleanup of temp paths, which the author addressed in the 2026-09-02 push

result.card: This PR (furszy) hardens the wallet's legacy-to-sqlite migration path so that exceptions and filesystem errors during migration fail gracefully instead of crashing or leaving the wallet needing manual restoration from backup, following up on two earlier merged fixes for the same migration path (#34156, #34176). The strongest evidence of importance is ryanofsky's code review ACK stating the last commit provides a 'potentially significant benefit' by delaying deletion of the original database until the new one is confirmed built, though he flags it as a complexity tradeoff and suggests a simpler future redesign. The PR is currently Stale, labeled 'Needs rebase' with mergeable_state dirty, despite the author actively addressing a detailed round of review comments as recently as 2026-09-02. No open objections remain unaddressed; agreement is positive with an acknowledged, non-blocking complexity caveat. It has no hard dependencies, but conflicts with two other open wallet-migration PRs (#34909, #35436).
